title: How to Store Halloween and Fall Decor So You Can Actually Find It Next Year
description: An easy ADHD-friendly way to pack up Halloween and fall decor in one evening, plus 7 Amazon storage finds so next year starts in minutes, not hours.
intro:
Every year it goes the same way. You buy a cute skeleton. You love the skeleton. November arrives, the skeleton goes into "a box somewhere," and next October you buy a new skeleton because the old one has left this plane of existence.

If that's you, welcome. Our brains are great at decorating and not so great at the boring packing-up part. And when the packing up is chaos, next year's decorating starts with an hour of digging through the garage.

This year, let's flip it. Here's a simple way to pack up Halloween and fall decor so future-you opens one bin and smiles. Plus seven Amazon finds that make it easier.

sections.heading: Before you pack: the 10-minute keep-or-go
sections.body:
Before anything goes into a bin, grab a trash bag and a donate bag and set a 10-minute timer.

- **Broken?** Trash. You will not glue it.
- **Didn't put it out this year?** It probably won't come out next year either. Donate.
- **Melted candle, crushed garland, bald wreath?** Let it go.

You don't have to be ruthless. You only have to stop paying rent on stuff you didn't use. Every item you skip packing is one less item to dig through next fall.

sections.heading: One season, one color
sections.body:
Pick a bin color for each season or holiday. Orange or black lids for Halloween and fall, red or green for winter holidays, and so on.

This is a gift to our brains. You don't have to read a label in a dim garage. You see orange, you know it's October. Color does the remembering for you.

sections.heading: Pack by where it goes, not by what it is
sections.body:
Tidy-people advice says sort by type: all the candles together, all the garland together. For us, it works better to pack by **where it lives in the house**.

One bin for the front porch. One bin for the mantel. One bin for the kitchen table. Next year you carry the porch bin to the porch, open it, and you're done. No sorting, no wandering around holding a pumpkin wondering where it went last year.

sections.heading: Snap a photo before you take it down
sections.body:
Before you pack the mantel, take one photo of it. Then tape a printed copy (or a sticky note saying "see photo in phone album: Fall Mantel") inside the bin lid.

Next year there's no decision fatigue about where things go. You copy last year's photo. Our brains love a picture way more than a plan.

sections.heading: Wrap the fragile stuff the easy way
sections.body:
Skip the tissue paper origami. Wrap breakable pieces in the dish towels, tablecloths and fabric runners you're packing anyway. Two jobs, one step.

For small ornaments and mini pumpkins, an egg-carton-style ornament box keeps them from rolling into a sad pile at the bottom.

sections.heading: Give the bins a home you can reach
sections.body:
Seasonal bins don't need prime real estate, but they need a *findable* spot. A high garage shelf, the top of a closet, under a guest bed. Put all seasonal bins in one zone so "where are the holiday things?" has one answer.

And label two sides of every bin. Whichever side faces out, you can read it.

sections.heading: Tiny tip: the 'first out' pouch
sections.body: Put a zip pouch on top of each bin with the stuff you always need first: extension cord, hooks, command strips, spare batteries for the light-up pieces. Next year you open the bin and everything to *start* is right there.

finds.why: Your wreath keeps its shape and hangs on a hook instead of getting crushed under a bin.

outro:
Packing up isn't the fun part. But one calm evening now means next fall you open a bin, copy a photo and you're done before your coffee gets cold.
